item.title: China's grain industry annual output value to exceed 4.5 trln yuan during 2026-2030
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
Home>>
China's grain industry annual output value to exceed 4.5 trln yuan during 2026-2030 (Xinhua) 13:48, September 21, 2026
BEIJING, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- The annual industrial output value of China's grain industry is expected to exceed 4.5 trillion yuan (666.8 billion U.S. dollars) during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), an official said on Monday. The grain sector will better meet people's demand for higher-quality, more nutritious and healthier food, said Liu Huanxin, head of the National Food and Strategic Reserves Administration, at a press conference. (Web editor: Zhang Kaiwei, Liang Jun)

item.title: China, U.S. have candid, in-depth, constructive exchanges during consultations on economic, trade issues
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
China, U.S. have candid, in-depth, constructive exchanges during consultations on economic, trade issues NEW YORK, Sept. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese and U.S. teams on Sunday held candid, in-depth and constructive exchanges during consultations on economic and trade issues. Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, who led the Chinese delegation, held economic and trade talks in New York with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, head of the U.S. side, and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer. Guided by the important consensus reached by the heads of state of the two countries, they have engaged in exchanges on important economic and trade issues of common concern, as well as the implementation of consensus reached in previous talks, by upholding the principles of mutual respect, peaceful coexistence and win-win cooperation. They also held dialogues on AI-related issues. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Xiplomacy: Five years on, China's Global Development Initiative delivers tangible progress
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
Xiplomacy: Five years on, China's Global Development Initiative delivers tangible progress BEIJING, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- "Stay committed to putting development first, and open up the prospects for shared prosperity." At the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit in Bishkek this year, Chinese President Xi Jinping once again called on countries to make development a priority. In September 2021, Xi proposed the Global Development Initiative (GDI) at the 76th session of the UN General Assembly, bringing a vision of shared development to the global agenda and calling for the benefits of development to be more widely shared. Five years on, the initiative has evolved from a vision into concrete cooperation, with more and more countries joining forces in the pursuit of a better future for all. FROM VISION TO SHARED ASPIRATION The GDI was put forward at a critical moment when the global development agenda was facing unprecedented challenges. In the Sustainable Development Goals Report 2021, the United Nations underscored the scale of the setback: global extreme poverty rose for the first time in more than 20 years, with 119 million to 124 million people pushed back into extreme poverty in 2020, while 101 million children fell below the minimum reading proficiency level. It was against this background that Xi proposed the development initiative, emphasizing the necessity to put development high on the global macro policy agenda. The initiative calls for staying committed to development as a priority, to a people-centered approach, to benefits for all, to innovation-driven development, to harmony between man and nature and to results-oriented actions. "It was both timely and strategically far-sighted. At a time when the international agenda is increasingly dominated by differences and dividing lines, the initiative brings a fundamental question back into focus: how to achieve development and stability and create a dignified future for people," said Serik Korzhumbayev, editor-in-chief of the Delovoy Kazakhstan newspaper. In January 2022, when the Group of Friends of the GDI was launched at the UN Headquarters in New York, delegates from more than 100 countries attended the meeting, voicing support for the initiative and willingness to join the group. "Development holds the key to people's well-being." Over the past five years, Xi has continued to promote the implementation of the initiative at the SCO, BRICS, the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation, the G20 and other multilateral platforms, calling for building political consensus to ensure everyone values development and all countries pursue cooperation together. "This is where I see particular value in the GDI: it links development with people, and national needs with the shared responsibility of the international community," Essam Sharaf, former Egyptian prime minister and founder and chairman of the Sharaf Foundation for Sustainable Development, told Xinhua. As of now, nearly 100 countries and international and regional organizations have signed cooperation documents with China on the initiative, while the Group of Friends of the GDI has grown to 88 countries. Reflecting on the GDI's progress over the past five years, Abdulaziz Alshaabani, a Saudi researcher at the Al Riyadh Center for Political and Strategic Studies, said the initiative "has evolved from a Chinese proposal into concrete mechanisms for international cooperation." "One noticeable change since the launch of the GDI is that more and more countries have begun to place development and related issues higher on the international cooperation agenda," said Alshaabani. PROGRESS IN ACTION In Rwinkwavu, a rural area in Kayonza district of Rwanda's drought-prone Eastern Province, a bank of solar panels enclosed by a blue fence stand among the hills. The solar-powered borehole is one of 200 drilled under a China-funded project benefiting about 110,000 people across the province. Magnifique Habimana, head teacher of GS Rwinkwavu school, one of the beneficiaries, told Xinhua that "the project came at the right time to address a serious water problem." "It was a very big inconvenience to the school in terms of sanitation and running costs," said Habimana. Over the past five years, stories like this have unfolded in communities across the developing world. While projects involving infrastructure, energy and water have made everyday life easier, agricultural cooperation has expanded to more than 140 countries and regions, with over 1,000 agricultural technologies shared with developing countries and more than 14,000 technicians trained in hybrid rice technology. "For developing countries, development is not an abstract political formula. It means new roads and railways, reliable energy supplies, modern enterprises, jobs, education, digital connectivity, food security, access to technology and better prospects for the younger generation," Korzhumbayev told Xinhua. Backed by more than 23 billion U.S. dollars in funds it has mobilized, the initiative has implemented over 1,800 "small and beautiful" projects and trained more than 200,000 professionals, delivering concrete benefits to local communities in over 120 countries. At the SCO Bishkek Summit, Xi announced plans to implement 100 technological cooperation projects with other SCO countries in the next three years and nurture more green industry talents through China-SCO cooperation, building on his pledge a year earlier at the SCO Tianjin Summit that "China plans to implement 100 'small and beautiful' livelihood projects in member states with such need." A defining feature of the GDI is its emphasis on action and tangible results, said Hussein Askary, vice-chairman of the Belt and Road Institute in Sweden. "China not only discusses development issues, but also takes concrete action to advance common development." A PATH FORWARD Five years on, development remains as an urgent priority as ever, as geopolitical conflicts, economic uncertainty and climate change compound the pressing challenges facing the international community. The latest UN data show that only 36 percent of the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) targets with available trend data are on track or making moderate progress, and 15 percent have even regressed below their 2015 baselines. "This is precisely why, in my view, the significance of the GDI has actually increased over the past five years," said Emin Gasimov, director of Azerbaijan's Center for the Study of China's Global Initiatives, Development and Culture. While emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), are creating new development opportunities, they also pose a risk of widening existing gaps. Sharaf noted that the GDI presents a major opportunity to help shape an important principle for the next phase. "The future of technology should not be a future for a limited number of countries, but a shared future for humanity," he said. Xi has described AI as "a new engine of world economic growth and an accelerator for the shift of growth drivers." As a new round of technological revolution and industrial transformation gathers pace, he has called for bridging the digital and AI divides, so that technological revolution and development achievements can benefit all nations. In July, during the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance in Shanghai, an upgraded version of MAZU was officially handed over to Djibouti, marking a new step in China-Djibouti cooperation on AI-powered climate resilience. MAZU, short for multi-hazard, alert, zero-gap and universal, is an AI-driven meteorological early warning platform developed by China and named after the Chinese guardian goddess of the sea. Currently, MAZU has been deployed on the ground in seven countries and is providing cloud-based services in more than 40 countries, making it an important international public good serving countries across the Global South. At the 2026 WAIC, Xi announced that China will provide developing countries with 5,000 opportunities in AI training and seminar programs in the next five years, and said that 30 countries can use the AI-powered meteorological warning system to safeguard homes around the world. Projects such as MAZU offer a stellar example of how digital technologies can support the implementation of the GDI, said Alshaabani. "Its value lies not simply in providing a technology, but in helping countries strengthen their capacity for disaster early warning, risk management and emergency response." Beyond MAZU, China has been building a broader framework for international AI cooperation, including establishing the World AI Cooperation Organization with 28 other countries and setting up international AI application cooperation centers with major regional and multilateral organizations. If such emerging technologies can be made more accessible to the Global South, the role of the GDI will expand significantly, Alshaabani told Xinhua. "It will not only help developing countries address today's development challenges, but also help them build the capacity to adapt to future technological change." "In my view, this is one of the most promising transformations of the GDI: from development assistance to jointly building the capacity to develop. For the Global South, this capacity could become one of the most important resources of the next decade," said Gasimov. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: Xi replies to U.S. university students
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
Xi replies to U.S. university students BEIJING, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping recently replied to students from 10 U.S. universities who wrote to him after attending youth exchanges in China. Xi noted that he was delighted to learn that the students enjoyed a pleasant and memorable journey in China. Xi said he was pleased to hear that the students expressed in the letter their appreciation for Chinese civilization, their hope for friendly cooperation between China and the United States, and their willingness to act as envoys of friendship bridging the Pacific Ocean. Young people from China and the United States, Xi said, share the same planet Earth and jointly shoulder the mission of the times. He expressed hope that the students would join the vast number of young people in both countries in striving to carry forward, uphold, and advance China-U.S. friendly cooperation, and work together to foster mutual understanding and affinity between the two peoples and to ensure the steady and long-term development of bilateral relations, so as to contribute the vitality of youth to building a better world. Recently, nearly 100 students from Harvard University and nine other U.S. universities wrote to Xi, sharing their experiences and what they had gained from the Future Makers 2026 China-U.S. Youth Tour for a Shared Asia-Pacific Future and other exchange events in China, and expressing their willingness to contribute to promoting China-U.S. friendship. item.title: Xi to pay state visit to U.S. from Sept. 23 to 25
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
Xi to pay state visit to U.S. from Sept. 23 to 25 BEIJING, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping will pay a state visit to the United States from Sept. 23 to 25 at the invitation of U.S. President Donald Trump, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced on Monday. During the visit, Xi and Trump will have an in-depth exchange of views on major issues concerning China-U.S. relations and world peace and development, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said at a regular news briefing. Head-of-state diplomacy plays an irreplaceable role in providing strategic guidance for China-U.S. relations, and the exchange of visits between the two heads of state within six months marks a historic milestone, Guo said. China is ready to work with the U.S. side to enrich the connotation of the constructive relationship of strategic stability, enhance dialogue and cooperation, properly manage differences, and continuously contribute to the well-being of both peoples and global peace, stability and prosperity, he added. item.title: China-Africa cooperation in vocational education builds skills, opens opportunities
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
China-Africa cooperation in vocational education builds skills, opens opportunities Tola Tsegaye Alemu (R) from Ethiopia operates an industrial robot under the guidance of a teacher in Tianjin University of Technology and Education in north China's Tianjin, June 27, 2024. (Xinhua/Sun Fanyue) * The skills that carried African competitors to skills competitions like the World Vocational College Skills Competition are among the everyday subjects in classrooms that China and Africa run together. For some, success in competition has opened the door to employment. * Young Africans across the continent are gaining practical skills as China-Africa cooperation in vocational education continues to grow. For many, mastering a skill is ultimately about finding a job, or even starting a business. The longer game is not training one class of students, but enabling African schools to train their own. WINDHOEK, Sept. 20 (Xinhua) -- In a workshop in Ongwediva, northern Namibia, fabric rustles as Wilhemina Amadhila measures, cuts and stitches. "Each stitch comes together to form a stunning outfit," said the 22-year-old woman who will take the craft to the 48th WorldSkills Competition to be held on Sept. 22-27 in Shanghai, China. Amadhila and 16 other young Namibians will compete in different categories of the competition. Besides Namibia, other African countries such as Kenya, Egypt, South Africa and Morocco are also taking part in the contest to showcase their technical and vocational skills. This is not the first time African competitors have taken part in skills competitions in China. Their active participation offers a glimpse of growing China-Africa cooperation in vocational education, which has helped endow many Africans with practical skills and opportunities. This photo taken on Nov. 14, 2025 shows a scene at the final of the World Vocational College Skills Competition in Tianjin, north China. (Xinhua/Zhao Zishuo) LEARNING THROUGH PRACTICE At the 2025 World Vocational College Skills Competition held in north China's Tianjin, Angolan student Massak Ventura Noquena Eduardo took silver on the strength of industrial robotics and automated production-line skills learned from Chinese teachers. "I hope to apply what I have learned to Angola's industrialization," he said. The skills that carried him to the podium are among the everyday subjects in classrooms that China and Africa run together. At the Angola-China Institute of Technology, students study mechatronics, industrial robotics and automation. Guo Xiaoyu, a teacher from Baotou Vocational and Technical College in north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, remembers students who were at first hesitant to even use a multimeter or an oscilloscope. "Vocational education cannot be based on theory alone. Students have to do things with their own hands," Guo said. After a semester of practice in circuit assembly and fault diagnosis, more than 90 percent of them met the required standard. At Ethiopia's Holeta Polytechnic College, Chinese instructor Ma Yujie demonstrated surgical suturing as animal science students gathered around the table, taking turns practicing on training pads. "We are now participating in practical demonstrations," Lemi Abera, 22, said. "With our Chinese instructors linking classroom concepts to practical animal health practices." A contestant operates a computer numerical control machine during a vocational skills challenge at the Technical University of Kenya in Nairobi, Kenya, Aug. 29, 2025. (Xinhua/Yang Guang) Ma is one of 20 Chinese teachers working at six vocational colleges across Ethiopia. "The students really cherish the opportunities to practice on training models, to the extent that some are willing to spend extra time in the laboratory after class," she said. In Cameroon, the classroom has moved onto the construction site. In early August, China First Highway Engineering Co., Ltd. teamed up with Cameroon's Ministry of Higher Education and the National Advanced School of Public Works to run the country's first certification course for surveyors. Cameroon's Minister of Higher Education Jacques Fame Ndongo said the program turns construction sites into "open-air classrooms" and builds a direct bridge between universities and major projects. This cooperation is not just about building roads; it is about training people, and about the future of Cameroon's workforce, the minister added. According to an action plan released at the 2024 Beijing Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation, China will continue vocational education with Africa, build with African countries schools of engineering technology, set up or upgrade 10 Luban Workshops, and offer 60,000 training opportunities aimed chiefly at African women and youth. China has established 17 Luban Workshops in 15 African countries and trained tens of thousands of professionals. This photo taken on Feb. 15, 2024 shows a view of the Ethiopian Luban Workshop in a vocational training institute in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. (Xinhua/Li Yahui) FROM SKILLS TO LIVELIHOODS For many young Africans, mastering a skill is ultimately about finding a job, or even starting a business. At the end of 2025, 30 Rwandan students came home from a year of advanced training at Jinhua University of Vocational Technology in east China's Zhejiang Province. Aimable Tuyishime, a 23-year-old e-commerce graduate who studied logistics, warehouse management and data analysis there, is now building an online shopping platform for Rwandan consumers. "This is the right time to put all the skills and experience I gained into practice," he said. In Tanzania, the Kilimanjaro Institute of Technology and Management launched a Chinese culinary program early this year, combining video lessons from chefs in China with practice in local kitchens. "These are skills that make you different, and I can even start my own restaurant one day," said hospitality student Ruth Washima Seni. For some, success in competition has opened the door to employment. At last year's Namibian national skills contest, the gold medalists in cooking and restaurant service also won three-month apprenticeships with a local hospitality group. SEEDS THAT STAY The longer game is not training one class of students, but enabling African schools to train their own. In Cote d'Ivoire, seven modern vocational schools built by Chinese contractors opened last September. Spanning some 83,000 square meters, they can take about 5,600 students in 15 trades, from machining to auto repair and agro-processing. Moreover, 184 Ivorian teachers and administrators from the schools spent four months in China learning to use and maintain equipment, while 15 school managers studied school management there. Two Chinese vocational institutions now help operate five of the schools. In Kenya, China-supported vocational education cooperation is entering a new phase: 69 institutions will receive equipment for 70 training workshops, and 1,190 instructors and technicians will be trained in both countries. "A trained instructor can train many generations of trainees; (and) a modern workshop can continuously produce skilled workers," said Esther Thaara Muoria, principal secretary of the State Department for Technical and Vocational Education and Training in Kenya's Ministry of Education. Wu Jiashun, who heads the central Africa regional center of China First Highway Engineering, put it more plainly: a young person trained today will work for 30 years, and will bring up more young people along the way. "That is how a country learns to build its own roads." For Amadhila and her teammates, Shanghai will be more than a place to compete. It will serve as a global classroom where they can test their skills, learn from their peers and bring new ideas home. Behind these young Africans are more classrooms like these, where young people across the continent are gaining practical skills as China-Africa cooperation in vocational education continues to grow. item.title: China's new-generation synchrotron radiation facility achieves first beam
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
China's new-generation synchrotron radiation facility achieves first beam An aerial drone photo taken on Sept. 16, 2026 shows the Hefei Advanced Light Facility (HALF) under construction in Hefei, east China's Anhui Province. (Xinhua/Zhou Mu) HEFEI, Sept. 20 (Xinhua) -- The linear accelerator of the Hefei Advanced Light Facility (HALF) successfully generated and delivered an electron beam on Sunday, marking a key step forward in the construction of the world's most advanced fourth-generation synchrotron radiation facility in the low-energy range. Located in Hefei, capital city of east China's Anhui Province, the institution is a fourth-generation synchrotron radiation facility operating at a designed energy of 2.2 gigaelectronvolts (GeV) and based on diffraction-limited storage ring technology. It is also a major national science and technology infrastructure project in China. By generating highly intense and coherent light, the facility will serve as a "super microscope" for scientists to probe the microscopic structure of matter. Compared with third-generation synchrotron radiation sources, HALF is expected to produce soft X-rays with more than 100 times higher brightness and coherence. It will enable the development of experimental techniques with greater precision and sensitivity in the spatial, temporal and energy domains, providing an important research platform for studying microscopic particle behavior, the structure of light elements, and changes in the electronic, chemical and spin states of materials. This photo taken on Aug. 27, 2026 shows the linear accelerator of the Hefei Advanced Light Facility (HALF) under construction in Hefei, east China's Anhui Province. (Xinhua/Zhou Mu) "Successful beam generation and delivery means that we have taken a key step toward the ultimate goal. The electron beam produced by the linear accelerator is the source of synchrotron radiation. Its beam quality, stability and reliability directly affect the performance of the storage ring and the downstream beamlines and experiments," said He Zhigang, chief engineer of the injector system. The project will next enter a critical stage of commissioning, during which the electron beam will be injected into the storage ring. The facility will gradually move toward full-system commissioning and stable operation, He said. Once completed, HALF will become an internationally advanced fourth-generation synchrotron radiation facility in the low-energy range and complement existing synchrotron radiation sources in China by covering a different energy range. It is expected to provide an experimental platform for cutting-edge research in materials science, life sciences and energy science, and contribute to research in areas including high-temperature superconductivity, new energy batteries, aerospace, biomedicine and advanced materials. According to He, once completed, HALF will be open to scientists from both China and abroad, providing a shared research platform for advanced studies in fields such as quantum information, energy, environment and life sciences. item.title: CPC leadership meeting studies major issues on Party self-governance, sets dates for Party plenum
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
CPC leadership meeting studies major issues on Party self-governance, sets dates for Party plenum BEIJING, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on Monday chaired a meeting of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, which studied major issues on strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance and set the dates for an upcoming Party plenum in October. The meeting decided that the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the CPC will be held from Oct. 26 to 29 in Beijing. The meeting also decided to submit a document on the CPC Central Committee's decision regarding strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance to the plenum for deliberation. An earlier draft of the decision was circulated among Party members and non-Party figures for comment, drawing broad support from those consulted. The meeting noted that the document provides an objective assessment of the achievements and experience in advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance in the new era, offers an in-depth analysis of the situation and tasks facing Party building in the present and coming period, and sets out strategic plans for continuing to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance. The meeting stressed that, to strengthen full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance, it is imperative to uphold the Party's overall leadership and the centralized, unified leadership of the CPC Central Committee, maintain a strict approach without wavering, and improve the systems for exercising full and rigorous self-governance. Efforts must be made to ensure that the Party remains a vibrant Marxist governing party that stays at the forefront of the times, enjoys the wholehearted support of the people, withstands all tests, and serves as the strong leadership core in building socialism with Chinese characteristics, said the meeting. The meeting called for fully recognizing the significance and urgency of unswervingly advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance, adopting higher standards and taking more concrete measures to address the prominent issues facing Party building.
